name: Proxemics
citation: Hall, E.T. (1966). The hidden dimension. Anchor Books.
rejection_rationale: Collapses into Privacy Regulation (Altman) + Spatial Navigation (SN framework). Hall's four distance zones (intimate, personal, social, public) are fully explained by IC interoceptive boundary management + SN peripersonal space coding. No independent T1.5 residual remains after this decomposition.

provenance.historical_context: Edward T. Hall, a cultural anthropologist, coined the term 'proxemics' in 1963 and defined it as the interrelated observations and theories of humans' use of space as a specialized elaboration of culture. His foundational work formalized a notation system for proxemic behavior. The Hidden Dimension (1966) provided comprehensive theoretical exposition, emphasizing proxemic behavior's impact on interpersonal communication. Hall categorized personal space into four distinct zones: intimate (0-18 inches), personal (18 inches to 4 feet), social (4-10 feet), and public (10+ feet). Key innovation: proxemic behavior is largely culturally conditioned, with biological underpinnings paralleling animal territoriality.
key_milestones: 1963: Hall coins 'proxemics' term and develops notation system
1980s-Present: Applications in communication, architecture, organizational psychology, HCI
provenance.current_status: foundational in intercultural communication; active research on cultural dimensions and digital/virtual space applications
